thread:
jamie: Heads up — noticed a ~25% tokens/sec drop in prod starting ~22:10 UTC after the rollout. Dashboard: https://internal.perf/graphs/abc123

deploy-bot: deploy redwood/runtime@release-2026-03-17 finished by @maria at 22:08 UTC :white_check_mark:

alex: same here in canary. throughput flat until ~1200 token mark then falls off sharply. latency p50 ok, p95 and p99 spike.

priya: I ran a quick profile on a repro. KV cache hitrate unchanged. CPU memcpy spikes align with the drop. suspect kernel selection mismatch causing fallback copies.

jamie: thanks. stacktrace-ish from top run:
```
# perf top snippet
  memcpy                32.4%
  runtime_batcher       12.1%
  cuMemcpyAsync         11.8%
  kernel_fp16_attention 9.3%
```

dan: that memcpy % is suspicious. the new batching heuristic change (merge 5f3a7a) switches the scheduler to prefer narrow-time windows which may reorder requests longer than expected. if kernel selection sees odd sequence lengths it routes to a fallback kernel that does extra memcopies.

alex: I bisected locally. reverting commit 5f3a7a+ changes the token/sec goes back to normal on same repro.

priya: confirmed. quick bisect log:
- baseline (old): 2400 tok/s
- post-merge 5f3a7a: 1780 tok/s
- revert batch-window heuristic: 2380 tok/s

ev an: (typo: evan) I've uploaded a flamegraph: https://s3.internal/fg/2123456789-flame.svg — shows memcpy hot path through kernel adapter. Kernel decision path picks 'small-window-optimized' kernel for some batches that are actually long, so it ends up copying and reshaping.

maria: rolling hold on release? sales already flagged a customer.

oncall-bot: paging @eng-oncall (pri): high-sev perf regressions detected, action required.

priya: I'll open a revert PR and a follow-up to tighten the kernel-selection guard (check aggregated seq_len distribution across coalesced batch before mapping kernel).

jamie: plan: 1) hold rollout 2) revert 5f3a7a now 3) patch heuristic + add unit/integration perf test covering long-run batch coalescing 4) smoke test in canary 5) resume.

dan: note: also add assert to scheduler metrics to emit avg_seq_len_in_window — would help detect in CI.

alex: quick patch idea: if avg_seq_len_in_window > 1024 prefer large-kernel path, avoid reshape+memcpy. I'll draft.

maria: thanks all. @priya please post revert PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

priya: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/432-revert-batcher-heuristic — reverting the heuristic and adding integration perf test. cc @maria

jamie: verified canary after revert: tokens/sec back up. scheduling rollback to prod.

alex: follow-up todo: add e2e that simulates mixed short+long sequences under continuous-batcher to catch this.

maria: good triage. reopen if regressions persist. :eyes:
